rationale: Ground truth's substantive concerns are the AllGather-KV packed-metadata breakage (P1) and the exact-aligned-input SAGE-disable bug (P2), both later patched by follow-up commits. X reviews the tree as if these are all resolved, lists them as '[resolved]' without engaging their nuance, and spends most of its output on test-coverage/doc nits (CI lane gaps, missing unit tests) that are grounded but low-value and don't probe the actual mechanisms reviewers cared about. Y validates the same two fixes are present but goes further: it traces the exact-aligned-suffix trim fix, critiques the AllGather-KV reject as overly broad/name-based and proposes a narrower query_ranges-based fix (directly engaging bobboli's open FA4+AllGather-KV question), and surfaces new, concretely-demonstrated bugs (unvalidated max_seqlen_q/k, all-false-mask zero-token launch, SAGE gate ignoring q_block_size) with runnable counterexamples and precise line-anchored fixes. Neither has a LATENT GAP CHECK section, so gap_hit is false for both. Y is more grounded, more actionable, and covers materially more of the reviewers' actual concern space.
